stages.name: Along the route
stages.desc: Lands the ship sailed past: Hittite Anatolia and its vassals

stages.name: Copper source
stages.desc: Alashiya (Cyprus): mines and smelters of the oxhide ingots

stages.name: Glass & luxury producer
stages.desc: Egypt: glass, gold, ebony and ivory from Nubia and beyond

stages.name: Canaanite ports
stages.desc: City-kingdoms of the Levant where cargoes were gathered

stages.name: Mycenaean destination
stages.desc: Palaces of the Aegean that bought metals and luxuries

stages.name: Wreck site
stages.desc: The coast where the ship sank, off Uluburun near Kaş

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Alashiya: copper mines of the Troodos foothills feed smelters at Enkomi and Kalavasos
The king of Alashiya sends copper to Pharaoh and calls him 'my brother'
Some ten tons of Cypriot copper sink with the Uluburun ship

states.name: Israel
timeline: Canaanite cities under Egyptian rule; the port of Tell Abu Hawam ships goods by sea
Canaanite kings write to Pharaoh from Megiddo and Akko

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Canaanite hill towns and coastal trade under Egyptian rule
Abdi-Heba of Jerusalem writes to Pharaoh for archers

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Byblos, Sidon and Tyre: ports of cedar, purple dye and Canaanite jars
Rib-Hadda of Byblos begs Pharaoh for help as Amurru closes in

states.name: Syria
timeline: Ugarit, the richest port of the Levant, gathers goods from inland and overseas
Suppiluliuma conquers Syria; Ugarit becomes a Hittite vassal but keeps trading

states.name: Turkey
timeline: The Hittite kingdom rules central Anatolia; its south coast is the sea road west
Suppiluliuma I takes the Hittite throne
A merchant ship carrying copper, tin and glass sinks off Uluburun

states.name: Greece
timeline: Mycenaean Greeks rule Knossos; mainland palaces import metals and luxuries
Mycenae, Tiryns, Pylos and Thebes grow rich on trade and war

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Egypt of the 18th Dynasty: glass furnaces, gold from Nubia, ebony and ivory from the south
Amenhotep III comes to the throne; Egypt's wealth and diplomacy reach their height
Akhenaten and Nefertiti build a new capital at Amarna
Tutankhamun abandons Amarna and restores the old gods
General Horemheb becomes pharaoh

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Enkomi, the island's great port, casts copper into oxhide ingots
Enkomi's workshops and harbour ship copper across the sea

events.title: Mycenaeans at Knossos
events.text: Mycenaean Greeks now rule Knossos on Crete and keep its accounts in Linear B.

events.title: An alphabet in clay
events.text: Scribes at Ugarit write a cuneiform alphabet of thirty signs for trade and ritual.

events.title: Copper of Alashiya
events.text: Smelters at Enkomi cast Cypriot copper into four-handled oxhide ingots.

events.title: Amenhotep III
events.text: Amenhotep III begins a reign of peace and splendour paid for with Nubian gold.

events.title: The Aegean List
events.text: A statue base at Amenhotep III's temple names Mycenae, Knossos and Nauplion.

events.title: Kommos harbour
events.text: Crete's southern port receives Canaanite jars, Cypriot pottery and Egyptian wares.

events.title: Royal glass
events.text: Palace workshops at Malkata colour glass with cobalt to imitate lapis lazuli.

events.title: Mycenaeans on Rhodes
events.text: Mycenaean settlers at Ialysos give the Aegean a stepping-stone toward Cyprus.

events.title: Miletus
events.text: Mycenaean Greeks hold Miletus, the Hittites' Millawanda, on the Anatolian coast.

events.title: Treasury of Atreus
events.text: Mycenae's rulers build great vaulted tombs for their dead.

events.title: Akhenaten
events.text: Amenhotep IV succeeds his father and soon renames himself Akhenaten.

events.title: Nefertiti
events.text: Nefertiti becomes great royal wife and shares the king's new worship of the Aten.

events.title: Suppiluliuma
events.text: Suppiluliuma I takes the Hittite throne at Hattusa.

events.title: Alashiya's copper
events.text: The king of Alashiya sends Pharaoh copper and asks for silver in return.

events.title: Tell Abu Hawam
events.text: A Canaanite harbour under Mount Carmel trades with Cyprus and the Aegean.

events.title: Amarna founded
events.text: Akhenaten builds Akhetaten, a new capital on empty desert ground.

events.title: Letters to Pharaoh
events.text: Canaanite kings write to Egypt in Akkadian on clay; the Amarna letters survive.

events.title: Megiddo
events.text: Biridiya of Megiddo reports raids and asks Pharaoh for troops.

events.title: Jerusalem's plea
events.text: Abdi-Heba of Jerusalem warns that the land of the king is being lost.

events.title: Fire at Ugarit
events.text: A letter from Tyre reports that half of Ugarit's palace has burned.

events.title: Hittites in Syria
events.text: Suppiluliuma sweeps through Syria; Mitanni's power is broken.

events.title: Washukanni sacked
events.text: The Hittites sack the capital of Mitanni, Egypt's old ally.

events.title: Ugarit turns Hittite
events.text: King Niqmaddu II of Ugarit becomes a Hittite vassal but keeps his fleet.

events.title: Byblos besieged
events.text: Rib-Hadda of Byblos writes letter after letter for help as Amurru closes in.

events.title: Akhenaten dies
events.text: Akhenaten dies; Nefertiti may briefly rule as pharaoh.

events.title: Tyre's island
events.text: Abi-Milku of Tyre complains he has no water or wood on his island city.

events.title: Kadesh falls
events.text: Kadesh on the Orontes passes from Egypt's orbit to the Hittites.

events.title: Amarna abandoned
events.text: Tutankhamun leaves Amarna and restores the old gods.

events.title: Carchemish taken
events.text: The Hittites take Carchemish and make it their stronghold on the Euphrates.

events.title: Tin from the east
events.text: Caravans carry tin from Central Asia toward the ports of Syria.

events.title: Tutankhamun dies
events.text: The young king dies; an Egyptian queen asks Suppiluliuma for a husband.

events.title: Plague in Hatti
events.text: Suppiluliuma dies of a plague brought home by Egyptian prisoners.

events.title: Mycenae's palaces
events.text: Mycenae, Tiryns and Pylos buy copper, tin, glass and ivory from the east.

events.title: The ship sails
events.text: A heavily laden ship leaves a Levantine port, westbound for the Aegean.

events.title: Uluburun
events.text: The ship strikes the rocks off Uluburun and sinks in forty to sixty metres of water.

events.title: Horemheb
events.text: The general Horemheb becomes pharaoh and erases the Amarna kings from memory.

events.title: Arzawa conquered
events.text: Mursili II conquers Arzawa in western Anatolia; its capital Apasa, later Ephesus, falls.

events.title: Thebes in Boeotia
events.text: Mycenaean Thebes stores eastern treasures, among them seals of lapis lazuli.

events.title: Troy VI falls
events.text: An earthquake or war destroys the great walled city of Troy VI.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's eastern Mediterranean countries, by each one's main part in the Uluburun cargo. Borders are modern; every land both bought and sold, and the map shows only its leading role. Egypt and Anatolia are vast and swing the shares. Dates are approximate.
